metadata.case_name: DING KWOK KEUNG v. MORETIDE INVESTMENTS LTD

injuries.description: mild sprain back without neurological complication
source: Both experts agreed that the plaintiff suffered a mild sprain back without neurological complication.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of lumbar spine

injuries.description: mild posterior disc bulging at L4/5 with mild compression at the anterior thecal sac (clinical impression PID at L4/5)
source: MRI of the lumbar spine was performed on 10 December 2014 which showed mild posterior disc bulging at L4/5 level, with mild compression at the anterior thecal sac. The clinical impression was PID at L4/5.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis

manifestations.description: persistent pain in his low back, usually with a sense of tightness requiring stretching
marked decrease in lumbar flexion movement
limited tolerance (about an hour) in walking, standing and sitting
impaired capacity in handling heavy weight
shaking of the lower limbs on climbing stairs
numbness at the plaintiff’s upper limbs (not related to the accident)

treatments_received.treatment: A&E attendance and assessment at Princess Margaret Hospital
source: he attended the A&E Department of Princess Margaret Hospital (“PMH”) for treatment of his back pain after work. Physical examination at the A&E Department revealed that his pain was located at the lower lumbar region without local swelling. But there was marked decrease in lumbar flexion movement.
he was then referred to physiotherapy for treatment, which he attended from 9 October 2013 to 26 February 2014 for a total of 11 sessions.

The plaintiff was assessed by the occupational therapist at CMC on 24 March 2014. An intensive course of training started on 26 March 2014 at frequency of 3 sessions per week. During the period between 24 March 2014 to 31 October 2014, the plaintiff attended a total of 90 sessions of occupational therapy.
he also attended outpatient physiotherapy at CMC for treatment of his persistent back pain from 28 August 2014 to 28 October 2014 for a total of 9 sessions.

MRI of the lumbar spine was performed on 10 December 2014 which showed mild posterior disc bulging at L4/5 level, with mild compression at the anterior thecal sac. The clinical impression was PID at L4/5.
